summary: EmberLine is a web app that turns 25 years of NASA satellite fire detections into one consistent burning activity calendar for any area on Earth. MODIS (2000–) and VIIRS (2012–) see fires at different resolutions, so their hotspot counts cannot be compared directly: VIIRS finds about 4 times more hotspots in the same fires. We translate both sensors onto one scale with region-, season- and day/night-specific ratios, and we test those ratios on years they never saw. The calendar then shows emergency managers, land managers and scientists when an area typically burns, which years were worst, and whether this month is unusual. It also shows how confident each number is. We built it for our home, Johor, which is hit by haze from Sumatran peat fires, but it works everywhere.
details:
What it does. Pick an area from the presets, a country, a point and radius, a box, or a polygon drawn on the map, and optionally a date range. EmberLine shows:

  • a year-by-month burning activity calendar from 2000 to the present, coloured by anomaly (percentile against a baseline you choose) or by hotspot count
  • annual totals, a monthly median row and the critical period (the shortest run of months that holds 75% of typical burning)
  • the status of the latest month (pro-rated while the month is still in progress), how the current year ranks so far, the long-term trend (Theil–Sen with Mann–Kendall significance) and any shift in fire-season timing
  • a harmonization confidence rating for the selected area, based on how closely MODIS and VIIRS agreed there in 2012–2023, so users know how much to trust the estimated pre-2012 years
  • a plain-language brief, a printable one-page version and a shareable link
  • downloads for the selected area and date range: monthly and annual harmonized series as CSV (with 80% intervals, sources and percentiles), every chart as a PNG image, and the raw FIRMS hotspots detected in the area for any dates since 2000 (up to 31 days per request, using the visitor's own free FIRMS key; standard-processing data where available, near-real-time after)

How it works.

  1. Clean: we read every hotspot in the FIRMS standard-processing archives (MODIS C6.1 Terra/Aqua, VIIRS 375 m S-NPP/NOAA-20; 549 million detections). We keep only vegetation fires (type 0) with nominal or high confidence, which removes volcanoes and gas flares.
  2. Grid: we count hotspots on a 0.25° grid by month, satellite and day/night.
  3. Learn the ratios: in the overlap years we learn VIIRS-to-MODIS ratios per 5° region × calendar month × day/night. Partial pooling shrinks ratios in data-poor regions toward regional and global values, and cross-validation chooses the pooling strength.
  4. Translate: MODIS years (2000–2011) are translated to the VIIRS scale. Terra-only months (Nov 2000 – Jun 2002) are first lifted to Terra+Aqua. NOAA-20 continues the record after Suomi NPP's retirement in November 2026 and fills partial Suomi NPP months that the pipeline detects automatically (Jul–Aug 2022, Jul and Nov 2024).
  5. Validate and quantify uncertainty: in leave-one-year-out cross-validation, our ratios cut the median error of country-month estimates from 30% (single global ratio) to 20%, with a correlation of 0.96. Residuals give an error model that puts an 80% interval on every estimated month.
  6. Catch sensor problems: the data itself shows Terra's orbit drift (the Terra/Aqua ratio fell from 0.53 to 0.41 after 2023). EmberLine stops using MODIS as a reference after 2023.

Up to date. The record runs from November 2000 to 13 November 2026. For 2026, VIIRS NOAA-20 standard-processing data is used through July and near-real-time data after that, with static industrial sources removed statistically. With this data, EmberLine shows that Central Kalimantan's 2026 season is already the 3rd most active since 2001, behind only 2006 and 2015, and that November is running far above normal.

Benefits.

  • Responders can check in seconds whether conditions are unusual for their area.
  • Managers can plan patrols and burn bans around the critical period.
  • Scientists get a sensor-consistent series with honest uncertainty.

In our Riau (Sumatra) example, the calendar picks out June 2013, the month of the record Singapore–Johor haze, as the most active month on record, without being told.

Source code: https://github.com/sleeplessLh/emberline (Apache-2.0).

Tools. Python, DuckDB, pandas and NumPy for the pipeline; JavaScript, D3 and Leaflet for the web app; GitHub Pages for hosting. It is a static site with no server, so it is cheap to run and easy to mirror.
